Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

## Overview
Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire/Stimulus) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Runtime & Deployment (`bin/serve`)
- Started via `bin/serve` with `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Plain HTTP (`assume_ssl = false`, `force_ssl = false`), accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`), serves static assets directly from Puma (`public_file_server.enabled = true`).
- Health check at `GET /up` (unauthenticated, returns `200`).
- All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) reside under `storage/`.

## Domain Model (Release 1: Quiz Preparation)
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required). `has_many :questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, `has_many :active_questions`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (1-indexed integer). `has_many :options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
  - `save_with_option_rows(question_attrs, raw_rows)`: skips blank option rows, validates `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and `>= 1` correct option among non-empty rows (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`). On failure, rolls back / avoids DB writes and preserves exact user-entered rows on `@question.form_option_rows`.
  - `move_up!` / `move_down!`: swaps adjacent siblings inside `quiz.with_lock` and compacts positions `1..n`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `text` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (1-indexed integer). Multiple correct options per question are supported.

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- All controllers under `Moderate::` inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Auth against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Stimulus controllers:
  - `option_rows_controller.js`: dynamically appends/removes and renumbers option rows (`Option N` / `Option N is correct`) on the question form.
  - `auto_submit_controller.js`: persists `"Active"` checkbox changes immediately (`fetch` with `keepalive: true`) and updates active counts and numbering in place.
  - `preview_controller.js`: stateless in-browser preview of active questions (`Question X of Y`, `Correct!` / `Wrong!`, reveals `.is-correct` options, `Next question` / `See score` -> `Score: X/Y` / `Start over`), storing nothing on the server.

## Design Assets & Future Screens
- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` come from `docs/mockups/`.
- `quizzy.css` already includes component styles for upcoming releases:
  - Big screen presentation: `.cover`, `.screen`, `.screen-controls`, `.lobby`, `.qr`, `.counter-pill`, `.stage-question__*`, `.stage-options`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader`.
  - Audience mobile play: `.play`, `.join-form`, `.waiting`, `.play-question__*`, `.play-options`, `.play-option`, `.play-status`, `.result-card`, `.winner-banner`.
  - Moderator game runs & responses: `.runs-table`, `.badge`, `.tabs`, `.response-options`, `.response-card`.

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` -> `Moderate::QuizzesController#export`, `Quiz#export_payload` / `Quiz#to_export_json`):
  - Linked via `"Export"` on the quiz page (`/moderate/quizzes/:id`).
  - Renders pretty-printed JSON inside the single `<pre class="code-block">` on the page.
  - Writes **only** `title` and `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` -> `text`, `correct`), always writing `active` and `correct` booleans and preserving `(position, id)` order. Future features (such as game runs, participants, or responses) must **never** add extra keys to `export_payload`.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import` -> `Moderate::QuizImportsController`, `Quiz::Import`):
  - Linked via the `"Import quiz"` button on `/moderate`.
  - Form has `"Quiz JSON"` textarea and `"Import"` submit button.
  - Defaults `active` to `true` and `correct` to `false` when omitted; preserves `questions` and `options` order; enforces the same rules as the quiz/question forms (`title` present, question `text` present, `>= 2` non-blank options, `>= 1` correct option).
  - Always creates a new `Quiz` (even when a quiz with the same title already exists) inside a single DB transaction after full pre-validation; on any error, re-renders with `422` and imports nothing.

  end

  def join_url(fallback_base_url = nil)
    effective_base = fallback_base_url.presence || base_url.presence || "http://localhost:3000"
    "#{effective_base.sub(%r{/\z}, '')}/play/#{code}"
  end

  def qr_svg(fallback_base_url = nil)
    qrcode = RQRCode::QRCode.new(join_url(fallback_base_url))
    qrcode.as_svg(
      color: "000000",
      fill: "ffffff",
      shape_rendering: "crispEdges",
      module_size: 8,
      standalone: false,
      use_path: true,
      viewbox: true,
      svg_attributes: {
        role: "img",
        "aria-label" => "QR code"
      }
    ).html_safe
  end

  def stream_token
    Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game).generate(id)
  end

  def self.find_by_stream_token(token)
    game_id = Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game).verified(token)
    find_by(id: game_id) if game_id.present?
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless lobby?

      active_qs = quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).to_a
      now = Time.current

      if active_qs.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          started_at: now,
          finished_at: now,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      else
        active_qs.each_with_index do |q, q_idx|
          gq = game_questions.create!(
            question_id: q.id,
            body: q.body,
            position: q_idx + 1
          )
          q.options.each_with_index do |opt, o_idx|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              option_id: opt.id,
              text: opt.text,
              correct: opt.correct?,
              position: o_idx + 1
            )
          end
        end

        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: now,
          question_opened_at: now,
          question_closed_at: nil,
          state_version: state_version + 1
        )
      end
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless question_open?

      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        question_closed_at: Time.current,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next unless question_closed?

      total = game_questions.count
      next if current_question_index + 1 >= total

      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: current_question_index + 1,
        question_opened_at: Time.current,
        question_closed_at: nil,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_quiz!
    changed = false
    with_lock do
      next if finished?

      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: Time.current,
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_all! if changed
    changed
  end

  def submit_answer!(player:, option_id:, client_seq: 0)
    result = nil
    gq = nil

    with_lock do
      if !question_open? || player.nil? || player.game_id != id
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      gq = current_game_question
      if gq.nil?
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      option = gq.game_options.find { |o| o.id == option_id.to_i }
      if option.nil?
        result = { accepted: false }
        next
      end

      answer = gq.game_answers.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id)
      seq = client_seq.to_i

      if answer.persisted? && seq > 0 && answer.client_seq > 0 && seq < answer.client_seq
        result = { accepted: true, question_id: gq.id, picked_option_id: answer.game_option_id }
        next
      end

      answer.game_option_id = option.id
      answer.client_seq = [ seq, answer.client_seq.to_i ].max
      answer.answered_at = Time.current
      answer.save!

      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
      result = { accepted: true, question_id: gq.id, picked_option_id: option.id }
    end

    if result[:accepted]
      broadcast_moderator!
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(
        "play_player_#{player.token}",
        {
          type: "player_answer",
          version: state_version,
          question_id: result[:question_id],
          picked_option_id: result[:picked_option_id]
        }
      )
    end

    result
  end

  def bump_version_and_broadcast_moderator!
    with_lock do
      update_columns(state_version: state_version + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
    end
    broadcast_moderator!
  end

  def moderator_payload(fallback_base_url: nil)
    reload_online_ids = online_player_ids
    online_count = reload_online_ids.size

    payload = {
      version: state_version,
      id: id,
      code: code,
      status: status,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      join_url: join_url(fallback_base_url),
      active_players_count: online_count
    }

    if question_open? || question_closed?
      gq = current_game_question
      if gq
        total = game_questions.count
        opts = gq.game_options.to_a

        if question_open?
          answered_count = reload_online_ids.empty? ? 0 : gq.game_answers.where(player_id: reload_online_ids).count
          payload[:question] = {
            id: gq.id,
            position: gq.position,
            total: total,
            last_question: gq.position == total,
            body: gq.body,
            answered_count: answered_count,
            options: opts.map { |opt| { id: opt.id, text: opt.text } }
          }
        else
          counts_by_option = gq.game_answers.group(:game_option_id).count
          total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
          payload[:question] = {
            id: gq.id,
            position: gq.position,
            total: total,
            last_question: gq.position == total,
            body: gq.body,
            total_answers: total_answers,
            options: opts.map do |opt|
              {
                id: opt.id,
                text: opt.text,
                correct: opt.correct?,
                answers_count: counts_by_option.fetch(opt.id, 0)
              }
            end
          }
        end
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def play_broadcast_payload
    payload = {
      type: "game_state",
      version: state_version,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status
    }

    if question_open? || question_closed?
      gq = current_game_question
      if gq
        total = game_questions.count
        payload[:question] = {
          id: gq.id,
          position: gq.position,
          total: total,
          body: gq.body,
          options: gq.game_options.to_a.map do |opt|
            item = { id: opt.id, text: opt.text }
            item[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
            item
          end
        }
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_state_payload(player)
    base = play_broadcast_payload.except(:type)

    if player.present? && player.game_id == id
      base[:joined] = true
      base[:player_name] = player.name
      base[:player_token] = player.token

      if base[:question].present?
        picked_id = GameAnswer.where(game_question_id: base[:question][:id], player_id: player.id).pick(:game_option_id)
        base[:question] = base[:question].merge(picked_option_id: picked_id)
      end
    else
      base[:joined] = false
      base.delete(:question) unless finished?
    end

    base
  end

  def broadcast_moderator!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("moderate_game_#{id}", moderator_payload)
  end

  def broadcast_players!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast("play_game_#{code}", play_broadcast_payload)
  end

  def broadcast_all!
    broadcast_moderator!
    broadcast_players!
  end

  private

  def assign_unique_code
    return if code.present?

    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      unless self.class.exists?(code: candidate)
        self.code = candidate
        break
      end
    end
  end
end

**Controller and View Design: A Deep Dive**

Okay, let's get down to brass tacks. We're building the controllers and views, and the Stimulus controllers that go with them, right? I want to make sure we're on the same page, so let's meticulously dissect the code.

**1. `Moderate::GamesController`:**  This controller is crucial for moderator actions. Because it inherits from `Moderate::BaseController`, every action is secured with HTTP Basic Auth, which is great.  The `show` action uses the `application` layout, same as the `Moderate::QuizzesController#preview` action – nice for consistency.  The `create` action handles game creation, and the `show` action dynamically updates the base URL for the join link if the moderator is accessing from a different network, which is smart. It also builds the payload with `moderator_payload`, generates the QR code, and assigns a stream token for the big screen. The HTML and JSON responses will be useful for different views. There are actions to start, finish, go to the next question, and end the quiz. All of these actions have the JSON/HTML fallback responses.

**2. `PlaysController`:** This is our public-facing controller; no moderator auth is required, so anyone can join.  It uses helper methods for browser-based player identification: `browser_token` (sets a cookie to uniquely identify the player) and `find_current_player` (uses the token from the cookie or the player's per-game cookie if available). This strategy makes sure the user is identified no matter what!  The `show` action is for displaying the game, and the `join` action handles new players. We need to handle potential race conditions when a user double-taps "Join" and ensure the game is finished. The `answer` action handles answer submissions and returns a JSON response to show the answer status.  The `state` action provides the game's current state (with an optional "offline_poll" parameter), which is a nice touch.  The `leave` action cleans up the player's presence, and, most importantly, we’re using `navigator.sendBeacon` and `FormData` for the leave action to avoid Brakeman warnings, and it is a good thing to do.

**3. Views & Stimulus Controllers – The Critical Match:**

Now, the really crucial part: making sure the DOM structure in the server-side ERB templates *exactly* mirrors the DOM structure managed by the client-side Stimulus controllers. This is where we ensure clean, flicker-free updates and avoid those pesky `ObsoleteNode` errors.

**A. Moderator Big Screen:**

We have a beautiful cover background color setup on the big screen that changes based on the game's state: lobby, question open, question closed, and finished. The goal is to make it look great with projectors.

**DOM Regions & Stimulus Controller:**

1.  `moderator-game` controller - The controller has several targets in its DOM structure:
    *   `lobbyView`: Hidden or shown depending on the game state (`status == "lobby"`).
    *   `questionView`: Hidden or shown when a question is open or closed.
    *   `finishedView`: Only shown when the game is finished.
    *   `topTitle` - Displays the quiz title if the game has started.
    *   `playersCounter` - Updates the number of players.
    *   `questionProgress`, `questionBody`, `questionOptions` - Displays the current question, progress, and options.
    *   `controlsJoinUrl` - Shows the join URL when questions are open/closed.

    refute_match(/correct/i, response.body)

class LiveGameEdgeCasesSystemTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  test "reloading phone mid-question preserves Your answer without leaking correctness, and unjoined guest sees live end" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Edge Case Live Quiz")
    q = quiz.questions.new
    q.save_with_option_rows(
      { body: "Which port is standard HTTP?", active: true },
      {
        "0" => { text: "Port 80", correct: "1" },
        "1" => { text: "Port 22", correct: "0" }
      }
    )

    join_url = nil
    big_screen_path = nil

    using_session(:moderator) do
      visit_moderate "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
      click_button "Start a game"
      big_screen_path = current_path
      join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
    end

    using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end

    # Guest opens join link but does NOT submit Join yet
    using_session(:unjoined_guest) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"
      page.execute_script("window.__guestNoReload = 'intact'")
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      # Unjoined guest is NOT counted as a player yet
      assert_text "Players: 1"
      click_button "Start"
      assert_text "Question 1 of 1"
      assert_text "Answers: 0 / 1"
    end

    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which port is standard HTTP?"
      click_button "Port 80"
      within("button", text: "Port 80") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end

      # Reloading phone mid-question remembers Alice AND her picked answer, and still leaks nothing about correctness!
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Which port is standard HTTP?"
      within("button", text: "Port 80") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
      refute_match(/correct/i, page.html)
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"

      # Reloading big screen mid-question renders exact open state
      visit_moderate big_screen_path
      assert_text "Question 1 of 1"
      assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"

      click_button "Finish"
      within("li", text: "Port 80") do
        assert_text "Correct"
        assert_text "1"
      end
      click_button "End quiz"
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
    end

    # Unjoined guest sitting on the join form live-transitions to "The quiz is over" without reload!
    using_session(:unjoined_guest) do
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_no_button "Join"
      assert_equal "intact", page.evaluate_script("window.__guestNoReload")
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Overview
Quizzy is a Rails 8.1 application (SQLite + Propshaft + Hotwire/Stimulus + Action Cable/Solid Cable) for running live conference talk quizzes.

## Runtime & Deployment (`bin/serve`)
- Started via `bin/serve` with `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Plain HTTP (`assume_ssl = false`, `force_ssl = false`), accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`), serves static assets directly from Puma (`public_file_server.enabled = true`).
- Health check at `GET /up` (unauthenticated, returns `200`).
- All SQLite databases (`primary`, `cache`, `queue`, `cable`) reside under `storage/`.

## Domain Model
### Quiz Preparation
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required). `has_many :questions` ordered by `(position, id)`, `has_many :active_questions`, `has_many :games`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required), `active` (boolean, default `true`), `position` (1-indexed integer). `has_many :options` ordered by `(position, id)`.
  - `save_with_option_rows(question_attrs, raw_rows)`: skips blank option rows, validates `>= 2` non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and `>= 1` correct option among non-empty rows (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`). On failure, rolls back / avoids DB writes and preserves exact user-entered rows on `@question.form_option_rows`.
  - `move_up!` / `move_down!`: swaps adjacent siblings inside `quiz.with_lock` and compacts positions `1..n`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `text` (required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (1-indexed integer). Multiple correct options per question are supported.

### Live Game
- `Game` (`games`): `quiz_id`, unique 5-char uppercase `code` (e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby` -> `question_open` <-> `question_closed` -> `finished`), `current_question_index`, monotonic `state_version`, `base_url`, timestamps (`started_at`, `question_opened_at`, `question_closed_at`, `finished_at`).
  - `start!` snapshots `@quiz.active_questions` (skipping inactive questions) and their `options` into `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`) and `GameOption` (`game_options`), isolating the running/completed game from future quiz edits while keeping optional `question_id` / `option_id` references (`on_delete: :nullify`).
  - Inline SVG QR code is generated locally via `rqrcode` (`Game#qr_svg`) encoding the exact same `join_url` displayed on the lobby screen.
- `Player` (`players`): `game_id`, `name` (required), `token` (unique), `browser_token` (unique per `game_id`, persisted in permanent signed cookies so reopening `/play/:code` in the same browser resumes as the same player while other games remain independent), `connections_count`, `online_until`.
  - `Player.currently_online` tracks players currently connected via `PlayGameChannel` WebSocket (`connections_count > 0`) or within a short HTTP grace window (`online_until > Time.current`) for initial page load and conference Wi-Fi HTTP fallback polling; `pagehide` beacon (`POST /play/:code/leave`) + WebSocket `unsubscribed` immediately mark disconnected tabs offline.
- `GameAnswer` (`game_answers`): unique per `(game_question_id, player_id)`, pointing to `game_option_id`, `client_seq`, and `answered_at`. Players can change their pick while `question_open?`; `client_seq` prevents delayed out-of-order conference Wi-Fi packets from overwriting a newer pick.

## Real-Time Channels & Security
- `ModerateGameChannel`: authenticates via HMAC-signed `stream_token` (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:moderate_game)`), streaming live state and player/answer counters to the moderator's big screen (`moderator_game_controller.js`).
- `PlayGameChannel`: streams public game state (`play_game_<code>`) and player-specific answer confirmations (`play_player_<token>`) to audience phones (`play_controller.js`).
- **Answer secrecy invariant**: While `status == "question_open"`, neither HTML source, JSON state endpoints, nor WebSocket broadcasts include option `correct` flags anywhere. `correct` booleans are only serialized once `finish_question!` transitions the game to `question_closed`.
- Both `moderator_game_controller.js` and `play_controller.js` combine Action Cable WebSockets with monotonic-versioned state reconciliation and lightweight background sync/retry for resilience on crowded conference Wi-Fi without page reloads.

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- All controllers under `Moderate::` inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic Auth against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Live game moderation lives at `/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games/:id` (`Moderate::GamesController`).

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` -> `Quiz#export_payload` / `Quiz#to_export_json`): writes **only** `title` and `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` -> `text`, `correct`), unaffected by games, players, or answers.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import` -> `Quiz::Import`): validates and atomically creates a new `Quiz`.
EOF

steps.message:
We have implemented the live quiz game feature for both moderators and players in Quizzy:

- **Moderator Live Game & Big Screen (`Moderate::GamesController`, `moderator_game_controller.js`, `ModerateGameChannel`)**:
  - Added the `"Start a game"` button on the quiz page (`/moderate/quizzes/:id`), creating a new independent `Game` with its own unique join code, players, and answers while keeping moderation under `/moderate`.
  - Before the start, the big screen displays the quiz title, the full join link as plain text, an inline SVG QR code (`rqrcode`) encoding the same link, the live `"Players: N"` counter of currently waiting players, and the `"Start"` button.
  - Clicking `"Start"` snapshots active questions (skipping inactive questions) and opens `"Question X of Y"` with live `"Answers: A / B"` (answered active players / active players currently in the game) and the `"Finish"` button.
  - Clicking `"Finish"` closes the question, reveals answer counts for every option, marks correct options with `"Correct"`, and shows `"Next"` (or `"End quiz"` on the last active question).
  - Clicking `"End quiz"` ends the game and displays `"The quiz is over"`.

- **Player Mobile Experience (`PlaysController`, `play_controller.js`, `PlayGameChannel`)**:
  - Joining via `/play/:code` asks for `"Your name"` with the `"Join"` button, greets waiting players with `"Hi, <name>!"`, remembers the player via persistent signed cookies across reloads in the same browser, allows joining at any time before the quiz ends, and shows `"The quiz is over"` (blocking new joins) after the end.
  - During open questions, options render as buttons that submit immediately on tap, mark the chosen option `"Your answer"`, allow changing picks until closed (last pick counts, guarded with `client_seq` ordering), and never expose correctness anywhere in HTML source, JSON endpoints, or WebSocket payloads before the question is closed.
  - After `"Finish"`, players see `"Correct!"`, `"Wrong!"`, or `"No answer"`, and after `"End quiz"`, `"The quiz is over"`, all live without page reloads and resilient to crowded conference Wi-Fi.
